source.title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection

claims.summary: Conventional RAG often retrieves a fixed number of passages regardless of need; unnecessary or off-topic passages can reduce versatility or generation quality.
Self-RAG trains one language model to retrieve on demand and to generate reflection tokens that evaluate retrieved passages and its own output.

locator.label: Figure 1
locator.selection: Retrieve-on-demand, parallel passage generation, critique, and segment selection flow

claims.summary: The paper argues that even a relevant retrieved passage does not by itself guarantee that the generated output will be consistent with that passage.

Self-RAG defines four reflection-token groups: Retrieve for retrieval timing, IsRel for passage relevance, IsSup for passage support of verifiable output statements, and IsUse for overall response utility.

locator.label: Table 1
locator.selection: All four reflection-token rows and their output values
locator.comparison_target: Roles of retrieval and critique tokens

claims.summary: At inference, Self-RAG either generates a segment without retrieval or retrieves passages, evaluates relevance, generates passage-conditioned candidates, evaluates support and utility, and ranks the candidates.

locator.label: Algorithm 1
locator.comparison_target: Self-RAG inference branches with and without retrieval

claims.summary: The critic training data is created by prompting GPT-4 for reflection-token labels; the authors collect roughly 4,000 to 20,000 supervised examples for each token type and distill them into an in-house critic.
The critic is initialized from Llama2-7B and reports over 90 percent agreement with GPT-4 predictions for most reflection-token categories.
The generator is trained with a standard next-token objective on outputs augmented with retrieved passages and reflection tokens; retrieved text chunks are masked from the training loss.
Retrieval can be triggered directly by the predicted Retrieve token or by comparing its normalized probability with an adjustable threshold.

For retrieved passages, Self-RAG uses segment-level beam search whose score combines generation probability with weighted IsRel, IsSup, and IsUse probabilities; undesirable critique outcomes can alternatively be hard-filtered.

The evaluation covers six tasks across short-form open-domain QA, closed-set fact verification and reasoning, biography generation, and long-form ASQA, using task-specific correctness, factuality, fluency, and citation metrics.
The final training setup uses 150,000 instruction-output pairs, Llama2 7B and 13B generator bases, and a Llama2-7B critic base.
The default retriever is Contriever-MS MARCO; biographies and open-domain QA add web-search passages, while ASQA uses author-provided GTR-XXL passages across baselines.
PopQA uses 1,399 rare-entity queries and TriviaQA uses an 11,313-query split; both are scored by whether a gold answer appears in the generated text rather than strict exact match.
The human evaluation samples 50 PopQA outputs and 50 biography outputs and checks plausibility-and-support plus agreement with predicted IsRel and IsSup tokens.
The authors note that depending on a proprietary model such as GPT-4 for feedback can increase API costs and reduce reproducibility, motivating distillation into an in-house critic.
After offline corpus augmentation, the final generator learns to emit reflection tokens itself and does not require the critic model at inference time.
Self-RAG 13B reports 55.8 PopQA accuracy, 69.3 TriviaQA accuracy, 74.5 PubHealth accuracy, and 73.1 ARC accuracy; Self-RAG 7B reports 54.9, 66.4, 72.4, and 67.3 respectively.

claims.summary: In the 50,000-instance training ablation, Self-RAG scores 45.5 on PopQA, 73.5 on PubHealth, and 32.1 ASQA string exact match, compared with 42.6, 72.0, and 18.1 when the critic is removed.

claims.summary: In the same ablation, always retrieving only the top-one passage scores 41.8 on PopQA and 28.6 on ASQA, while removing the IsSup score yields 44.1 and 30.6, below Self-RAG's 45.5 and 32.1.

claims.summary: Increasing the IsSup decoding weight on ASQA raises citation precision but lowers MAUVE, showing a support-versus-fluency trade-off in the displayed setting.

claims.summary: Across the tested 5k, 10k, 20k, 50k, and 150k training sizes, Self-RAG shows an overall upward trajectory on PopQA and ASQA citation precision, while PubHealth changes less consistently.
